hypothesis: The balanced-head candidate improved recall, macro-F1, and label-count alignment but inflated false positives because replacement sampling changed each binary label prior. Applying the exact unit-strength binary log-odds difference between original combined-train priors and the deterministic sampled priors to the learned head biases should restore calibration while preserving ranking and representation gains.

correction.formula: bias_delta[label] = logit(original combined-train positive rate) - logit(realized sampled positive rate)
correction.originalData: the same fixed 841 aligned + 204 targeted training rows
correction.sampleReproduction: the same inverse-frequency row weights, 1045 replacement draws, torch generator seed 44

inference: unchanged Product-18, global threshold 0.35, canonical max-two selector
